Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They sent me a lot of emails with guides. It was very easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write an email if you had questions. The UL global office were quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask if you have a question. The staff is very helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is a little lower than UCPH but it was nice taking into consideration that English isn't my first language.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teachers there had more freedom, which had both positives and negatives. A positive was that they had a lot of flexibility regarding the curicculum and a negative was that they could change stuff about the exam with short notice and that they weren't so focused on following the curicculum.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sociology of Gender in Popular Culture, International Organisations and Global Governance, Environmental Economics, Policy-Making in the European Union and Comparative European Policits

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Gender in Popular Culture, International Organisations and Global Governance and Environmental Economics.

Environmental Economics requires a little more work than the two others but it was very interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had gotten a rash on my body and I didn't know why. In the middle of the night I checked my mattress and found some kind of bugs on it (fleas I think). The reception was closed and I didn't want to sleep there so I found a hotel. The day after, I told the reception at the uni accomodation. I took a video of my mattress but the pest control guy didn't see anything on my mattress and didn't want to look at the video that I had taken. They changed my mattress but didn't want to reimburse me for the hotel and taxi.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sooo many clubs and societies <3

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different clubs and societies. There was one for every preference.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Outdoor Pursuits Club was really good! You paid five euros and could go climbing on the UL climbing wall up to four times a week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see Killarney, it is really worth a visit. + Arran Islands

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. It is very similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlyness. People are very talkative even if they don't know you

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare that exchange might be hard in the beginning when you haven't made friends yet
2. Go see as many places as possible while you're there (take CityLink and Expressway, not Dublin Coach, which is known for being delayed).
3. Joining one of the clubs is a good way to meet people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any at the moment

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My housing situation

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
